prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for the GLP-1 discovery, credited to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not weaken the scientific case, and the chair's summary shows that no member's concern was about mechanism or maturity. The achievement is a discrete, describable change in the field: proglucagon processing and incretin physiology, the identification of the biologically active truncated peptide, its actions on islets, appetite and the cardiovascular system, and then long-acting agonists whose effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes have been confirmed in independent trials. I weigh the unanimous opening placement as no evidence of merit. The merit is that the mechanistic and the therapeutic halves of this story are both complete and stable. The scientific core is Holst for physiology and secretion, Drucker for receptor biology and the therapeutic rationale, and Mojsov for the active peptide. A citation that names the physiology and the active form, and then states what it enabled, lets the prize acknowledge the therapeutic consequence without crediting an industrial development programme in a discovery prize.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains the real weakness, and round 1 did not remove it. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested, and Habener and, in the earlier proglucagon work, Bell are absent from the supplied credit list. Knudsen is outside the three-person cap, so a prize for the physiology will be read by some as honouring the hormone and not the medicines. None of us can verify the priority record from the supplied material and several members, myself included, are working from recollection. I asked in round 1 that the chair have the evidence for GLP-1(7-36) examined, and the chair's summary lists this as open and does not settle it. I therefore treat the third name as the one part of the configuration that rests on an assumption I cannot test. A further, smaller weakness is that solid evidence on the long-term durability of weight loss and on safety is still accumulating, although I do not think this changes the discovery.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius said that Holst and Drucker are secure under any resolution of the priority question, that Knudsen would be the strongest replacement if Mojsov cannot be defended, and that she sees no principled way to remove Holst or Drucker in favour of Knudsen. She proposed a separate part or a different year for the drug development.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of your argument, and it is where my round-1 reasoning ends up as well. Because Holst and Drucker are fixed, the only open question is the third slot, and there the choice is between a discovery name (Mojsov) and a development name (Knudsen). I follow your view that Knudsen is the right fallback if the active-peptide priority proves indefensible, and I would accept that substitution rather than drop to a pair. I do not agree that the dispute is serious enough now to make the substitution. A contested priority is not the same as a refuted one, and the active truncated peptide is the step that made the physiology pharmacologically usable. I would keep Mojsov for this year and be explicit that the fallback exists. I do not support your suggestion of a separate part for development in the same year, because it would add a second achievement to a prize that is already carrying the main attribution risk.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, questions whether Knudsen should be named if the prize is to reach the drugs, and whether a second part such as CAR-T could sit alongside GLP-1 given that GLP-1 already uses all three names.
responses.response: On Knudsen, I accept your point that naming her would force the removal of a discovery scientist and that no principled way exists to remove Holst or Drucker. That argument decides the question for me, and it moves me further from Knudsen in the preferred configuration than I was in round 1, when I said I would keep her in the discussion. On a second part, the arithmetic is decisive. The cap is three people in the whole configuration, so adding CAR-T means GLP-1 would be reduced to a pair or CAR-T to a single name, and neither is defensible. I therefore answer the chair's question directly: round 2 should treat single-part B033 as the working configuration. I also note, for the record, that the co-authorship between you and me is on dopamine neurons and Nurr1 and does not touch any candidate here, so I do not think it needs more than the disclosure we have both made.

responses.point: Linnarsson would not drop Rosenberg lightly from the CAR-T configuration, because his adoptive-cell-therapy work and the first gene-engineered T-cell trials established that a patient's cells could be treated as a drug. He considers the unresolved attribution question to be Eshhar and not Rosenberg.
responses.response: I have reconsidered my round-1 weighting. You are right that Rosenberg's trials are why CAR-T could be tested in patients, and that the harder fairness problem is Eshhar's chimeric-receptor concept, which none of the credited names covers. That strengthens my reason for keeping B039 as an alternative and not as a rival to B033 this year: a configuration of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg and a configuration of June and Sadelain would each be criticised for a different omission, and the committee has not settled which. My earlier point on solid-tumour limits, toxicity and manufacturing still stands as a maturity reservation, but I now regard attribution as the main reason to wait, not maturity. If that can be resolved, I would be willing to see it as a strong candidate in a coming year.

responses.point: Sandberg regards the impact of GLP-1 as real but notes that the long-term safety and durability of the obesity benefit are still being characterised, and she calls Mojsov's contested priority the weakest link of the trio while keeping her in.
responses.response: I accept the durability point and have added it to my reservations. I do not think it alters the discovery claim, because the effect on glycaemia and body weight during treatment, and the cardiovascular and renal outcome data, do not depend on what happens after discontinuation. I do not share the description of Mojsov as the weakest link in a way that should lead to replacing her. The question for me is whether the committee, in a discovery prize, can name the identification of the active peptide. If it cannot, the citation should drop the active-form wording and the configuration should become Drucker and Holst with the third slot reconsidered, and I would want that decision to be made explicitly and not by default through the cap.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide can be defended, and whether Habener or Bell should have a claim on the third slot ahead of her. I cannot verify the record from the supplied material.
Whether the committee prefers Knudsen to Mojsov as the third name if the discovery-side priority cannot be settled. I currently prefer Mojsov but accept Knudsen as the fallback.
Whether the CAR-T attribution (Eshhar, and then the choice between June and Sadelain and a trio including Rosenberg) can be settled in a way that would make B039 a better configuration than waiting.
Whether the long-term durability and safety of the obesity effect will qualify the retrospective assessment of the achievement.
statement.conflict_note: No change. My documented ties are to Ronald Evans (nuclear receptors, from my Salk period, and no formal mentor relationship confirmed), Johan Ericson, and co-authorship with colleagues Svenningsson (about twenty works on dopamine neurons and Nurr1, count not audited) and El-Manira (one work in 2009). None of these people is credited on a shortlisted ballot. I have no documented tie to Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Knudsen, Habener, Bell, June, Sadelain, Rosenberg, Hall, Schreiber or Sabatini. I would recuse myself if such a tie emerged.
